drivingQuestion: What does one owe a person who is accustomed to greet him?
outcomeNote: A single undisputed dictum with two prooftexts; no question is raised against it.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ בַּחֲבֵרוֹ שֶׁהוּא רָגִיל לִיתֵּן לוֹ שָׁלוֹם, יַקְדִּים לוֹ שָׁלוֹם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בַּקֵּשׁ שָׁלוֹם וְרׇדְפֵהוּ״. וְאִם נָתַן לוֹ וְלֹא הֶחֱזִיר — נִקְרָא ״גַּזְלָן״, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתֶּם בִּעַרְתֶּם הַכֶּרֶם גְּזֵלַת הֶעָנִי בְּבָתֵּיכֶם״.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Ḥelbo said» that «Rav Huna said: One who is aware that another» person «is accustomed to greet him» is not only obligated to return his greeting, but «he» must «greet him first, as it is stated: “Seek peace and pursue it”» (Psalms 34:15). «If» the other person «extended» his «greeting to him and he did not respond, he is called a robber, as it is stated: “It is you who have eaten up the vineyard, the spoils of the poor is in your houses”» (Isaiah 3:14). The only way to steal from a pauper who owns nothing is to rob him of his dignity by refusing to return his greeting.

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי חלבו, אמר רב הונא
moves.summary: the last dictum of the R' Ḥelbo–Rav Huna run: greet first the one who is accustomed to greet you
moves.about: the ruling that one must be first to greet a person accustomed to greet him, and that failing to return a greeting makes one a robber

moves.summary: Psalms 34:15 as warrant for taking the initiative
moves.about: scriptural warrant for being first to extend a greeting

moves.summary: Isaiah 3:14 as warrant for calling one who withholds a reply a robber — the only thing a pauper owns is his dignity
moves.about: scriptural warrant that one who fails to return a greeting is called a robber
